The pt2399-core board BEFORE it was populated: the bytes committed by aa5034b,
"pcb: KiCad project and empty 2-layer board for pt2399-core", which is the commit
that created it. Not re-authored.

THAT CLAIM IS PINNED IN CODE, NOT HERE. tests/pcb/empty-board-fixture.test.ts
holds the file's sha256 and fails if these bytes change, because a provenance
claim in prose is a transcription with a date on it. This file says where the
bytes came from; that one is what keeps the statement true.

WHY A COPY EXISTS AT ALL. The headless update tool refuses a board that already
holds footprints, so its tests need an EMPTY board, and they used to copy
circuits/pt2399-core/pt2399-core.kicad_pcb for that. Running the tool against
the committed board for real - a deliberate act, and the point of the tool -
filled it with 24 footprints, and every one of those tests then refused at
board-not-empty instead of reaching the guard it was written for: 25 tests red,
every one of them a false red.

The circuit's board is a MOVING artifact - an outline, tracks, a revision bump -
while what those tests need is a FIXED empty input. Asking one file to be both
is what produced the false reds, and it would produce them again at every later
task that changes the board.

This is NOT a reduced or synthetic board. It is the real board's own
configuration - the layer stack, the (setup) block and the DRC floors - which is
what makes the end-to-end test a test of this circuit rather than of a toy, and
what makes R8 (setup-block) establish something about this board rather than
about a hand-built input. The schematic and the .kicad_pro those tests use still
come from circuits/pt2399-core/.

STALENESS IS GUARDED, NOT TRUSTED, and the same test file holds that too: the
(layers) block must match the committed board's exactly both ways, no (setup)
entry of this file's may differ from the committed board's by value or by key,
and every entry the committed board has gained must be on an enumerated list of
the values KiCad writes out after a load-and-save. Read that file for what
happens when one of those fails - the answer is a deliberate decision, not a
wider list.
